sentences.text: This is sixth application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail to applicant- Nawal Singh in connection with Crime No. 359/2019 for the offence punishable under Sections of 363, 366, 366-A, 370-A, 372, 373, 376-C, 376-D, 109 of IPC and Sections 3,4,5,6,16 and 17 of POCSO Act, registered at Police Station Gormi, District Bhind (Madhya Pradesh).
T h e applicant is in judicial custody since 11/12/2020 in the aforementioned case.
The allegation against him is related to his involvement with other co-accused in sell, purchase and rape of the prosecutrix.
The prosecutrix has been examined as PW/1 before the trial Court.

In her examination-in-chief, the only reference, she gives against the applicant is that the other co-accused Nawal Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143510786/
1 took her to the house of the present applicant in Bhitarwar

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In her examination-in-chief she does not make any allegation of rape by the applicant or any kind of assistance in her kidnapping or rape.

Learned counsel for the State and the Objector while opposing the application for grant of bail have submitted that in 164 statement of prosecutrix, she has stated that the applicant herein took Rs.
8,000/- and sold her to co- accused Satish.
However, once the statement of prosecutrix is recorded before the trial Court, the 164 statement is rendered only as a previous statement.
In para 16 of her statement before the trial Court, she categorically says that applicant did nothing to her and it was the co-accused Jagdish who had sold her to co-accused Satish for Rs. 60,000/-.
In paragraph No. 48 also, she says that applicant has not done anything to her.

Therefore, from the plain reading of the prosecutrix's statement, it appears that besides taking the name of the applicant and that it was his house that the prosecutrix was married of to the co-accused Satish, there is no specific allegations against him.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant herein shall be enlarged on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial court.

(ATUL SREEDHARAN) JUDGE JPS/-
